title: Champion vs native Ascend aclnn (CANN 9.0.0), measured 2026-11-08

protocol.pypto_side: frozen remote_harness.py, latency_us = median per-round effective_us (PYPTO_BENCH=1)
protocol.aclnn_side: tools/aclnn_bench.py (pyacl + ctypes on libopapi.so): wall-clock per round (enqueue aclnn call(s) + acl.rt.synchronize_stream), median; executor fetched once, marked repeatable, reused across rounds. Both sides end-to-end wall clock including host dispatch.
protocol.shape_policy: m-tier shape {M:4096, N:4096}; dtype = champion's native contract dtype (bf16)

results.note: aclnn logProbOut [M,N] (required output) and dlogits storage follow the input dtype (bf16); our contract keeps fp32 outputs, so the aclnn side stores less precisely. zlossOut/lseForZlossOut are not optional in practice (null -> 161001); dummy buffers allocated, returnZloss=False.

convention: speedup_pypto_vs_aclnn = aclnn_us / pypto_us; >1 means the pypto champion is faster
